total_chol.elite_note: Optimal total cholesterol (TC) sits roughly 160-200 mg/dL. The TC-mortality relationship is U-shaped: both high and very low TC associate with increased all-cause/CVD mortality in cohort data, but very low TC (<~140-160) is usually a MARKER of underlying illness (malnutrition, liver disease, hyperthyroidism, chronic inflammation, occult cancer) rather than an independently harmful target, so low TC should trigger a workup for cause rather than an attempt to 'raise' it. TC is also a crude aggregate (HDL+LDL+~VLDL) — ApoB, LDL-C and non-HDL-C are better risk markers, and a high TC driven by high HDL is not equivalent to one driven by high LDL. Interventions below target LOWERING elevated TC (via the LDL fraction) toward the optimal band without over-treating; do not chase TC below ~160 in isolation.

diet_exercise.name: Replace saturated/trans fat with unsaturated fat (Mediterranean / Portfolio dietary pattern)
diet_exercise.how: Cut saturated fat to <7-10% of calories and eliminate industrial trans fat; swap butter/fatty meat/tropical oils for olive/canola oil, nuts, oily fish; emphasize vegetables, legumes, whole grains
diet_exercise.effect: Lowers TC and LDL-C; replacing ~5% of energy from saturated fat with polyunsaturated fat reduces LDL/TC and cardiovascular events in RCT/meta-analysis data
diet_exercise.caution: Dietary cholesterol itself has a modest effect in most people; total pattern matters more than any single food. Very-low-fat diets can lower HDL and raise triglycerides.

diet_exercise.name: Soluble/viscous fiber (oats/beta-glucan, psyllium, legumes, barley)
diet_exercise.how: Aim for ~5-10 g/day of viscous soluble fiber (e.g., 3 g oat beta-glucan or 7-10 g psyllium), increased gradually with fluids
diet_exercise.effect: Small-to-moderate reduction in TC and LDL-C (literature ~5% TC in enriched-diet trials); dose-dependent (~1-2 mg/dL TC per gram soluble fiber)
diet_exercise.caution: GI bloating/gas if increased too fast; take other medications separated from psyllium to avoid impaired absorption.

diet_exercise.name: Regular aerobic exercise plus weight loss if overweight
diet_exercise.how: 150+ min/week moderate aerobic activity; combine with modest caloric deficit to lose excess visceral fat
diet_exercise.effect: Modest TC/LDL lowering; more consistent effect on raising HDL and lowering triglycerides and body weight, which improves overall lipid profile
diet_exercise.caution: Effect on TC alone is small; benefit is largely secondary to weight loss and improved HDL/TG rather than a large direct TC drop.

supplements.name: Plant sterols/stanols (phytosterols)
supplements.how: ~2 g/day of sterol/stanol esters (fortified spreads, dairy, or capsules) taken with meals
supplements.effect: Reduces LDL-C ~8-10% and lowers TC correspondingly by blocking intestinal cholesterol absorption; additive to statins
supplements.caution: Modest TC effect; may slightly lower fat-soluble vitamin/carotenoid absorption. Avoid in sitosterolemia (rare).

supplements.name: Psyllium husk supplement
supplements.how: ~5-10 g/day (e.g., divided doses before meals) with adequate water
supplements.effect: Lowers LDL-C and TC (meta-analyses show significant LDL reduction, ~5% TC), via bile-acid binding
supplements.caution: Bloating, gas; risk of esophageal/GI obstruction if taken with too little fluid; separate from other drugs by 1-2 h.

supplements.name: Red yeast rice (monacolin K)
supplements.how: Standardized monacolin K product; monacolin K is chemically identical to lovastatin
supplements.effect: Lowers LDL-C ~15-25% (comparable to low-dose statin) with corresponding TC reduction
supplements.caution: Effectively an unregulated low-dose statin: same risks (myopathy, liver enzyme elevation, drug interactions) plus inconsistent/undisclosed monacolin content and possible citrinin (nephrotoxin) contamination. FDA treats high-monacolin products as unapproved drugs. Use only with clinician oversight and lipid/liver monitoring; do not combine with a prescription statin.

drugs.name: Statin (e.g., atorvastatin, rosuvastatin)
drugs.how: Prescription, physician-supervised; dose titrated to risk and LDL target (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor)
drugs.effect: Large, reliable reduction in TC and LDL-C and in cardiovascular events; first-line for elevated LDL/TC with elevated ASCVD risk
drugs.caution: Prescription/physician-supervised only. Myalgia, rare myopathy/rhabdomyolysis, transient transaminase elevations, small diabetes-risk increase; drug interactions (CYP3A4). Requires baseline and follow-up lipid/liver monitoring; avoid in pregnancy.

drugs.name: Ezetimibe
drugs.how: Prescription, physician-supervised; 10 mg/day, alone or added to a statin (blocks NPC1L1 intestinal cholesterol absorption)
drugs.effect: Lowers LDL-C ~18-20% (with corresponding TC drop); adds ~15-20% further LDL lowering on top of a statin and reduces events (IMPROVE-IT)
drugs.caution: Prescription/physician-supervised only. Generally well tolerated; rare myalgia and liver enzyme elevation (higher when combined with a statin).

drugs.name: Bempedoic acid
drugs.how: Prescription, physician-supervised; oral ATP-citrate lyase inhibitor, often for statin-intolerant patients or add-on to ezetimibe
drugs.effect: Lowers LDL-C ~20-30% as monotherapy (~40-50% combined with ezetimibe) with corresponding TC reduction; reduced MACE ~13% vs placebo in statin-intolerant patients (CLEAR Outcomes)
drugs.caution: Prescription/physician-supervised only. Can raise uric acid (gout) and has been associated with tendon rupture and small increases in liver enzymes; avoid in pregnancy.

peptides.name: ApoA-I mimetic peptides (e.g., D-4F/L-4F, CER-001, 5A peptide)
peptides.how: Experimental, investigational-only, medical supervision; designed to mimic HDL/ApoA-I and promote reverse cholesterol transport / cholesterol efflux
peptides.effect: Aimed at HDL function and reverse cholesterol transport rather than lowering total cholesterol per se; human trials have shown mixed/largely negative results on clinical lipid and inflammation endpoints — no established TC-lowering benefit
peptides.caution: NOT FDA-approved; experimental and requires medical/clinical-trial supervision. Efficacy unproven and trials have failed to show consistent benefit; safety not established outside trials (infusion/immunogenicity and unknown long-term risks). This peptide class does not reliably lower total cholesterol and should not substitute for evidence-based lipid therapy.

creatinine.elite_note: In the elite band, creatinine sits mid-range, signaling both preserved glomerular filtration AND adequate skeletal muscle mass. Because it is a two-sided marker, a low value often just means low muscle, and a high value can mean high muscle or true renal impairment. Interpret alongside cystatin C (muscle-independent) and eGFR before acting.

diet_exercise.name: Progressive resistance training + adequate protein
diet_exercise.how: 2-3x/week progressive loading, ~1.0-1.2 g/kg/day leucine-rich protein
diet_exercise.effect: builds/maintains muscle mass, nudging a low, muscle-driven creatinine up toward mid-range
diet_exercise.caution: does nothing (and is the wrong move) if creatinine is high from reduced kidney filtration

diet_exercise.name: Kidney-protective habits (steady hydration, moderate protein, avoid nephrotoxins)
diet_exercise.how: consistent fluids; ~0.8 g/kg protein if filtration is reduced; limit chronic NSAID use
diet_exercise.effect: protects filtration so a truly elevated creatinine trends down over time
diet_exercise.caution: acute dehydration or very high protein/creatine loading transiently raises creatinine without kidney injury

diet_exercise.name: Blood pressure, weight and glycemic control via aerobic exercise
diet_exercise.how: regular aerobic activity plus DASH/Mediterranean pattern
diet_exercise.effect: slows renal functional decline, keeping creatinine stable in range

supplements.name: Creatine monohydrate
supplements.effect: augments muscle mass/strength gains from training (supports the muscle axis of creatinine)
supplements.caution: predictably raises MEASURED serum creatinine ~0.1-0.3 mg/dL via metabolic conversion, NOT kidney damage; confirm with cystatin C if the number looks worse

supplements.name: Whey protein / essential amino acids
supplements.how: 20-40 g to meet the daily protein target, especially post-exercise
supplements.effect: supports lean mass underlying creatinine when dietary protein is short

drugs.name: SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g., dapagliflozin, empagliflozin)
drugs.how: prescription, for diabetic/proteinuric/chronic kidney disease indications
drugs.effect: slows CKD progression (DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY), preserving filtration long-term; expect a small benign creatinine bump in the first weeks
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; indicated for kidney/cardiometabolic disease, NOT for adjusting the number in a healthy person; risks include genital mycotic infection and volume depletion

drugs.name: ACE inhibitor or ARB (e.g., losartan)
drugs.how: prescription for hypertension or proteinuric CKD
drugs.effect: slows renal decline; a benign initial creatinine rise up to ~30% is expected and acceptable
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; monitor potassium and creatinine; not for people without an indication

peptides.name: CJC-1295 + ipamorelin (GH secretagogues)
peptides.how: no approved protocol; used experimentally to raise GH/IGF-1 and lean mass
peptides.effect: may modestly increase lean mass, which could raise a low muscle-driven creatinine; no trials target creatinine itself
peptides.caution: largely NOT FDA-approved / experimental; requires medical supervision; specific risks include insulin resistance, fluid retention/edema, and theoretical tumor promotion via elevated IGF-1

urea_nitrogen.elite_note: Elite BUN sits low-normal (9-16), reflecting good hydration, efficient renal clearance, and moderate protein turnover. BUN rises with dehydration, high protein intake, GI bleeding, catabolic stress, and renal impairment. A very low BUN can instead signal inadequate protein intake or reduced hepatic urea synthesis, so read it alongside creatinine and albumin.

diet_exercise.name: Optimize hydration
diet_exercise.how: consistent daily fluid intake unless clinically fluid-restricted
diet_exercise.effect: lowers a dehydration-driven BUN and is usually the fastest lever
diet_exercise.caution: over-hydration is harmful in heart failure and advanced CKD; individualize

diet_exercise.name: Moderate protein, shift toward plant sources
diet_exercise.how: ~0.8 g/kg/day if BUN is elevated; favor legumes/plant protein over large animal-protein loads
diet_exercise.effect: less urea generated from protein catabolism, lowering BUN
diet_exercise.caution: do not under-eat protein if muscle mass or albumin is also a concern

diet_exercise.name: Lower sodium and address catabolic stressors
diet_exercise.how: cut processed/high-salt foods; identify GI bleeding, prolonged fasting, or corticosteroid use
diet_exercise.effect: supports fluid balance and reduces reabsorption- and catabolism-driven BUN

supplements.name: Soluble fiber / resistant starch
supplements.how: increase dietary fiber; resistant-starch supplements studied in CKD
supplements.effect: diverts nitrogen to fecal excretion, modestly lowering blood urea
supplements.caution: may cause bloating; strongest evidence is in CKD populations, weaker in healthy people

supplements.name: Synbiotics / probiotics
supplements.effect: some trials show modest urea/BUN reduction via gut nitrogen handling
supplements.caution: results inconsistent and mostly limited to CKD cohorts

drugs.name: SGLT2 inhibitor or ACEi/ARB (renoprotective)
drugs.how: prescription for CKD, diabetes, or hypertension
drugs.effect: preserves kidney filtration (proven renal outcomes), indirectly helping a kidney-driven BUN over time
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; note that diuretics conversely RAISE BUN; not appropriate for tweaking BUN in a healthy person

uric_acid.elite_note: Elite uric acid sits in the low-normal 3.5-5.5 range, comfortably below the ~6.8 mg/dL saturation threshold where monosodium urate crystals form. Lower urate also tracks with lower insulin resistance and blood pressure; genuinely low levels are rarely a clinical concern in practice.

diet_exercise.name: Weight loss + DASH-style dietary pattern
diet_exercise.how: caloric moderation toward a healthy weight; DASH pattern rich in vegetables and low-fat dairy
diet_exercise.effect: meaningfully lowers serum urate; a meta-analysis of DASH RCTs showed significant urate reduction
diet_exercise.caution: avoid crash-fasting/ketogenic extremes, which transiently RAISE urate

diet_exercise.name: Cut fructose, sugar-sweetened beverages, and alcohol
diet_exercise.how: minimize sodas and fruit-juice concentrates; reduce beer and spirits especially
diet_exercise.effect: lowers urate production; alcohol (beer most) and excess fructose are consistently linked to higher urate/gout

diet_exercise.name: Lower purine load; add coffee and low-fat dairy
diet_exercise.how: cut organ meats, anchovies/sardines; 1-3+ cups coffee/day; include low-fat dairy
diet_exercise.effect: modestly lowers urate; coffee and low-fat dairy are urate-lowering/uricosuric in cohort studies

supplements.name: Vitamin C
supplements.effect: modestly lowers serum urate (RCT meta-analysis mean ~-0.35 mg/dL)
supplements.caution: effect is too small to treat established gout; high doses raise kidney-stone and GI-upset risk

supplements.name: Tart cherry (juice or extract)
supplements.how: ~1 cup juice or an equivalent concentrate/extract daily
supplements.effect: modest urate reduction (a 4-week trial showed ~19% drop) with lower CRP
supplements.caution: juice adds sugar; effects are inconsistent across studies

supplements.name: Quercetin
supplements.effect: lowered serum urate modestly in a small RCT
supplements.caution: limited data; may inhibit CYP enzymes and interact with medications

drugs.name: Allopurinol (xanthine oxidase inhibitor)
drugs.how: prescription; start <=100 mg/day and titrate to a target urate <6 (or <5) mg/dL
drugs.effect: robustly lowers urate; guideline first-line urate-lowering therapy
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; risk of severe hypersensitivity (screen HLA-B*58:01 in at-risk ancestries); start low and co-cover to avoid mobilization flares

drugs.name: Febuxostat (xanthine oxidase inhibitor)
drugs.how: prescription; start <=40 mg/day and titrate to target
drugs.effect: lowers urate, often reaching target more reliably than allopurinol
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; carries a cardiovascular-mortality signal (CARES trial, boxed warning); generally second-line

drugs.name: Uricosurics / adjuncts (probenecid; losartan, SGLT2 inhibitor)
drugs.how: prescription; useful when the patient also needs blood-pressure or glucose control
drugs.effect: probenecid lowers urate via URAT1 blockade; losartan lowers urate ~0.2-0.3 mg/dL; SGLT2 inhibitors modestly lower urate
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; probenecid raises kidney-stone risk (needs high fluid intake) and is avoided in poor renal function

albumin.elite_note: Elite albumin (4.4-5.0) reflects strong hepatic synthetic capacity, good protein nutrition, and low systemic inflammation. Because albumin is a NEGATIVE acute-phase reactant, a level held down by inflammation (high CRP/IL-6) will not rise on protein alone until the inflammatory driver is addressed; rule out liver disease and urinary/GI protein loss when it is low.

diet_exercise.name: Adequate high-quality protein
diet_exercise.how: ~1.0-1.2 g/kg/day (more if catabolic/older), leucine-rich complete-protein sources
diet_exercise.effect: raises albumin when inadequate intake was the limiter (nutrition trials in dialysis patients raised albumin)
diet_exercise.caution: little added benefit when the true limiter is inflammation or liver dysfunction

diet_exercise.name: Reduce systemic inflammation
diet_exercise.how: manage obesity, resolve chronic infection, stop smoking, adopt an anti-inflammatory diet
diet_exercise.effect: removes IL-6-driven synthesis suppression, letting albumin recover
diet_exercise.caution: requires identifying and treating the specific inflammatory source

diet_exercise.name: Alcohol moderation + resistance exercise
diet_exercise.how: minimize alcohol to protect hepatic synthesis; train regularly
diet_exercise.effect: supports liver synthetic function and an overall anabolic state

supplements.name: Whey protein or essential amino acids
supplements.how: 20-40 g/day to close a dietary protein gap
supplements.effect: raises albumin in malnourished or dialysis populations
supplements.caution: no benefit if protein intake is already adequate

supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (EPA/DHA)
supplements.effect: may lower inflammation, indirectly supporting albumin synthesis
supplements.caution: effect is modest and indirect; high doses can affect bleeding/anticoagulation

drugs.name: Human albumin infusion (acute clinical use only)
drugs.how: IV, physician-administered for defined indications (large-volume paracentesis, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatorenal syndrome in cirrhosis)
drugs.effect: transiently raises serum albumin and plasma oncotic pressure for those indications; does NOT durably fix underlying synthesis
drugs.caution: prescription / hospital-administered blood product; NOT a longevity or wellness intervention; overuse risks fluid overload. The durable lever is treating the underlying liver disease, inflammation, or protein loss.

grimage.elite_note: GrimAge acceleration is the residual after regressing DNAm GrimAge on chronological age; elite/optimal is a negative value (biologically younger than peers, e.g. roughly -2 to -5 years). Because GrimAge is trained on DNAm smoking pack-years plus surrogates of 7 mortality-linked plasma proteins (ADM, B2M, cystatin-C, GDF-15, leptin, PAI-1, TIMP-1), the strongest lever by far is never-smoking/smoking cessation, followed by low cardiometabolic and inflammatory burden.

diet_exercise.name: Smoking cessation / never smoking
diet_exercise.how: complete tobacco cessation; avoid all combustible/cannabis smoke
diet_exercise.effect: largest modifiable lever; current smokers run ~9 yr higher GrimAge2, and GrimAge declines ~0.14 yr per year of abstinence toward never-smoker levels over years
diet_exercise.caution: reversal is gradual over years and dose-dependent; heavy long-term smokers retain residual acceleration

diet_exercise.name: Aerobic exercise / raising cardiorespiratory fitness
diet_exercise.how: regular moderate-vigorous endurance training, 3+ sessions/week
diet_exercise.effect: lowers GrimAge acceleration; ~-0.6 yr PCGrimAge in a 6-mo cycling study, and active vs inactive ~-1.26 yr GrimAgeAccel in cohorts
diet_exercise.caution: small RCTs plus observational data; magnitude modest and fitness gains must be sustained

diet_exercise.name: High-quality diet, limited alcohol, adequate sleep
diet_exercise.how: Mediterranean/DASH/plant-rich pattern; minimize alcohol (esp. spirits); treat insomnia/short sleep
diet_exercise.effect: lowers GrimAge acceleration; plant-rich diet ~-0.66 yr GrimAge in an RCT, while heavy alcohol and insomnia/short sleep each raise it (~+0.7 to +1.5 yr)
diet_exercise.caution: mostly observational plus one diet RCT; alcohol effect is dose- and beverage-dependent (liquor worst)

supplements.name: Marine omega-3 (EPA/DHA)
supplements.effect: modestly lowers/slows GrimAge (GrimAge2 slowed in the DO-HEALTH RCT; pooled estimates around -0.3 to -1 yr)
supplements.caution: mild bleeding risk at high doses and with anticoagulants; choose oxidation-tested products

supplements.name: Daily multivitamin-multimineral
supplements.effect: modestly slows GrimAge accrual; ~-0.11 yr/yr vs placebo in the COSMOS RCT, larger in those with baseline acceleration
supplements.caution: small effect; benefit shown for a broad-spectrum multi, not megadoses of single nutrients

supplements.name: Vitamin D3
supplements.effect: little effect alone on GrimAge but additive when combined with omega-3 (and exercise) in DO-HEALTH
supplements.caution: avoid excessive dosing/hypercalcemia; benefit largely as part of a combination

drugs.name: GLP-1 receptor agonist (semaglutide)
drugs.how: prescription weekly semaglutide (a peptide drug, but FDA-approved)
drugs.effect: lowered epigenetic aging in a 32-wk RCT: PCGrimAge ~-3.1 yr, GrimAge V2 ~-2.3 yr
drugs.caution: PRESCRIPTION / physician-supervised only; evidence is a single RCT in HIV-associated lipohypertrophy; GI effects, pancreatitis risk, lean-mass loss

drugs.name: Metformin
drugs.how: prescription metformin (geroscience use is off-label)
drugs.effect: inconsistent for GrimAge; small PCGrimAge decreases in one HIV monocyte study but null in larger/longer trials
drugs.caution: PRESCRIPTION / physician-supervised only; off-label for aging; GI upset, B12 depletion, rare lactic acidosis in renal impairment

peptides.name: Recombinant human growth hormone + DHEA + metformin (TRIIM protocol)
peptides.how: physician-run thymus-regeneration regimen combining rhGH with DHEA and metformin
peptides.effect: GrimAge fell ~2 yr and persisted 6 mo after stopping, but only in a 9-person uncontrolled pilot
peptides.caution: NOT FDA-approved for aging (rhGH approved only for GH deficiency); experimental and physician-supervised; specific risks: insulin resistance/hyperglycemia, edema, arthralgia, and theoretical cancer promotion

peptides.name: Thymic peptide bioregulators (thymalin)
peptides.how: injectable thymus-derived peptide, annual short courses (Russian protocols)
peptides.effect: long-term mortality reduction reported, but no data validating any effect on GrimAge specifically
peptides.caution: NOT FDA-approved and unproven against epigenetic clocks; requires medical supervision; specific risks: unregulated source/purity, no Western RCT replication, unknown long-term immune effects

phenoage.elite_note: PhenoAge acceleration is the residual of DNAm PhenoAge on chronological age; elite/optimal is a negative value (biologically younger than peers). DNAm PhenoAge is a methylation surrogate of Levine's clinical-chemistry mortality model built from albumin, creatinine, glucose, log-CRP, lymphocyte %, mean cell volume, red-cell distribution width, alkaline phosphatase and white-cell count, so the elite profile is low systemic inflammation (low hsCRP), good glycemic control, low RDW and a healthy leukocyte/lymphocyte balance.

diet_exercise.name: Regular physical activity / exercise
diet_exercise.how: consistent moderate-vigorous activity (aerobic + resistance)
diet_exercise.effect: lowers PhenoAge acceleration; ~-1.7 yr PhenoAgeAccel in active vs inactive adults, with diet-by-activity interaction
diet_exercise.caution: largely observational; effect requires sustained activity and is attenuated by adiposity

diet_exercise.name: Caloric restriction / weight loss to cut adiposity and inflammation
diet_exercise.how: modest sustained energy restriction toward healthy body composition
diet_exercise.effect: improves PhenoAge's glucose/CRP inputs; in the CALERIE RCT 25% CR mainly slowed pace-of-aging (~2-3%) with a smaller/non-significant PhenoAge clock change
diet_exercise.caution: avoid undernutrition, muscle loss, and bone loss; PhenoAge clock itself moved less than pace measures

diet_exercise.name: Anti-inflammatory high-quality diet, plus limiting alcohol/smoking
diet_exercise.how: Mediterranean/DASH/plant-rich pattern; minimize alcohol; no smoking
diet_exercise.effect: lowers PhenoAge acceleration via reduced hsCRP and glucose; diet quality is inversely associated with PhenoAgeAccel while alcohol raises it
diet_exercise.caution: mostly observational associations; benefit is through the clinical inputs (CRP, glucose) rather than a proven clock-specific effect

supplements.name: Marine omega-3 (EPA/DHA)
supplements.effect: lowers/slows PhenoAge (RCT-supported; pooled estimates around -1.6 yr) and reduces hsCRP, a core PhenoAge input
supplements.caution: mild bleeding risk at high doses and with anticoagulants; choose oxidation-tested products

supplements.name: Daily multivitamin-multimineral
supplements.effect: modestly slows PhenoAge accrual; ~-0.21 yr/yr vs placebo in the COSMOS RCT
supplements.caution: small effect; shown for broad-spectrum multi, not high-dose single nutrients

supplements.name: Vitamin D3
supplements.effect: minimal alone but additive with omega-3 (and exercise) on PhenoAge in DO-HEALTH
supplements.caution: avoid excessive dosing/hypercalcemia; value mainly in combination

drugs.name: GLP-1 receptor agonist (semaglutide)
drugs.how: prescription weekly semaglutide (a peptide drug, but FDA-approved)
drugs.effect: largest reported PhenoAge signal: ~-4.9 yr in a 32-wk RCT, consistent with big drops in weight, glucose and hsCRP (all PhenoAge inputs)
drugs.caution: PRESCRIPTION / physician-supervised only; single RCT in a special (HIV) population; GI effects, pancreatitis risk, lean-mass loss

drugs.name: Metformin
drugs.how: prescription metformin (geroscience use is off-label)
drugs.effect: improves the glycemic input to PhenoAge; direct epigenetic effect inconsistent (PCPhenoAge fell ~3.5 yr in one small HIV study but was null in a 96-wk RCT)
drugs.caution: PRESCRIPTION / physician-supervised only; off-label for aging; GI upset, B12 depletion, rare lactic acidosis in renal impairment

peptides.name: Recombinant human growth hormone + DHEA + metformin (TRIIM protocol)
peptides.how: physician-run thymus-regeneration regimen combining rhGH with DHEA and metformin
peptides.effect: multiple clocks including PhenoAge fell in a 9-person uncontrolled pilot
peptides.caution: NOT FDA-approved for aging (rhGH approved only for GH deficiency); experimental, physician-supervised; specific risk: rhGH raises glucose/insulin resistance, which can paradoxically worsen PhenoAge's glucose input if uncontrolled, plus edema and theoretical cancer promotion

peptides.name: Pineal/thymic peptide bioregulators (epithalon, thymalin)
peptides.effect: claimed longevity/telomere effects, but no data validating any effect on PhenoAge specifically
peptides.caution: NOT FDA-approved and unvalidated against epigenetic clocks; requires medical supervision; specific risks: unregulated source/purity, no Western RCT replication, unknown long-term safety

hba1c.elite_note: Elite 4.6-5.3%. Under ~5.7% is non-diabetic; 5.3% and below reflects excellent glycemic control. Interpret with context: unusually low HbA1c can also reflect anemia, high RBC turnover, recent blood loss, or over-treatment/hypoglycemia rather than superior metabolic health.

diet_exercise.name: Carbohydrate-reduced / Mediterranean diet + 5-10% weight loss
diet_exercise.how: cut refined carbs & added sugar, emphasize whole foods, protein & fiber; target 5-10% body-weight loss
diet_exercise.effect: lowers HbA1c ~0.3-1.0% (larger short-term with low-carb)
diet_exercise.caution: if on insulin or sulfonylureas, monitor for hypoglycemia and adjust meds with a clinician; long-term adherence is the main limiter

diet_exercise.name: Structured aerobic + resistance exercise
diet_exercise.how: >150 min/week moderate-vigorous, combine cardio and strength; HIIT is effective
diet_exercise.effect: lowers HbA1c ~0.5-0.7% (up to ~0.9% when >150 min/wk)
diet_exercise.caution: screen for cardiovascular disease/retinopathy before vigorous training; progress gradually

diet_exercise.name: Post-meal walking & reduced sedentary time
diet_exercise.how: 10-15 min walk after meals; interrupt prolonged sitting hourly
diet_exercise.effect: blunts postprandial glucose; modest HbA1c benefit
diet_exercise.caution: safe for most; attention to footcare if peripheral neuropathy

supplements.name: Berberine
supplements.effect: lowers HbA1c ~0.5-0.7% (RCT meta-analyses)
supplements.caution: OTC nutraceutical; GI upset; inhibits CYP3A4 (interacts with statins, cyclosporine, many drugs); trial quality/heterogeneity variable and supplement quality unregulated; avoid in pregnancy/breastfeeding

supplements.name: Magnesium (glycinate/citrate)
supplements.effect: small HbA1c/fasting-glucose reduction, mainly with deficiency and ≥4 months use
supplements.caution: diarrhea at higher doses; reduce dose in renal impairment

supplements.name: Alpha-lipoic acid
supplements.effect: modest, inconsistent glucose-lowering; strongest data is for diabetic neuropathy, not HbA1c
supplements.caution: may add to glucose-lowering medications; possible GI upset

drugs.name: Metformin
drugs.how: 500-2000 mg/day, titrated; extended-release better tolerated
drugs.effect: lowers HbA1c ~1-1.5% in type 2 diabetes (less at near-normal levels)
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; GI effects, vitamin B12 depletion; avoid if eGFR <30

drugs.name: SGLT2 inhibitor (empagliflozin/dapagliflozin)
drugs.how: once-daily, physician-selected
drugs.effect: lowers HbA1c ~0.5-0.8% with added cardiovascular/renal benefit
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; genital mycotic infections, euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis, volume depletion

drugs.name: Acarbose
drugs.how: 25-100 mg with the first bite of each meal
drugs.effect: lowers HbA1c ~0.5%, targeting postprandial glucose
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; flatulence and GI symptoms are common and dose-limiting

peptides.name: Semaglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist)
peptides.how: weekly subcutaneous or daily oral, physician-titrated
peptides.caution: a peptide therapeutic that IS FDA-approved (Ozempic/Rybelsus) but prescription / physician-supervised only, not a self-directed peptide; risks: nausea/vomiting, pancreatitis, gallbladder disease; contraindicated with personal/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2

peptides.name: Tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist)
peptides.effect: lowers HbA1c ~1.8-2.4% plus substantial weight loss
peptides.caution: FDA-approved peptide (Mounjaro) but prescription / physician-supervised only; risks: GI effects, pancreatitis, gallbladder disease; same medullary thyroid carcinoma/MEN2 contraindication

peptides.name: Retatrutide (triple GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonist)
peptides.caution: NOT FDA-approved / investigational — available only through trials or gray-market sources; long-term safety not established, GI effects and transient heart-rate increase reported; requires medical supervision

glucose_fasting.elite_note: Optimal fasting glucose 72-90 mg/dL; 100-125 is impaired fasting glucose and ≥126 (repeated) is diabetic range. A single reading is noisy—confirm with repeat testing or CGM trends. Avoid over-suppression/hypoglycemia, especially on glucose-lowering agents.

diet_exercise.name: Low-glycemic Mediterranean / carbohydrate-reduced diet + weight loss
diet_exercise.how: reduce refined carbs, sugary drinks and late-night eating; emphasize fiber, protein, monounsaturated fats; lose 5-10% if overweight
diet_exercise.effect: lowers fasting glucose and improves insulin sensitivity
diet_exercise.caution: monitor for hypoglycemia if on insulin/sulfonylureas

diet_exercise.name: Regular aerobic + resistance exercise with post-meal walks
diet_exercise.how: 150+ min/week plus 2 strength sessions; short walk after evening meal
diet_exercise.effect: improves insulin sensitivity and lowers fasting glucose
diet_exercise.caution: gradual progression; screen high-risk individuals before vigorous exercise

diet_exercise.name: Consistent adequate sleep (7-9 h); treat sleep apnea
diet_exercise.how: regular sleep-wake schedule; evaluate for obstructive sleep apnea if snoring/daytime sleepiness
diet_exercise.effect: poor/short sleep and untreated apnea raise fasting glucose and insulin resistance; correcting them lowers it
diet_exercise.caution: formal sleep evaluation if apnea suspected

supplements.name: Berberine
supplements.effect: lowers fasting glucose (~0.5 mmol/L / ~9-10 mg/dL in meta-analyses)
supplements.caution: OTC nutraceutical; GI upset; CYP3A4 interactions (statins, cyclosporine, etc.); unregulated quality; avoid in pregnancy/breastfeeding

supplements.name: Magnesium (glycinate/citrate)
supplements.how: 250-400 mg elemental/day, especially if intake/serum is low
supplements.effect: modest fasting-glucose reduction, mainly with deficiency and ≥4 months use
supplements.caution: diarrhea at higher doses; reduce in renal impairment

supplements.name: Myo-inositol (± D-chiro-inositol 40:1)
supplements.effect: improves insulin sensitivity and lowers fasting glucose/insulin (best evidence in PCOS/insulin resistance)
supplements.caution: generally well tolerated; mild GI upset possible

drugs.name: Metformin
drugs.how: 500-2000 mg/day, titrated; extended-release preferred
drugs.effect: lowers fasting glucose by reducing hepatic glucose output
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; GI effects, B12 depletion; avoid if eGFR <30

drugs.name: SGLT2 inhibitor (empagliflozin/dapagliflozin)
drugs.how: once-daily, physician-selected
drugs.effect: lowers fasting glucose via urinary glucose excretion, with cardiorenal benefit
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; genital infections, euglycemic ketoacidosis, volume depletion

peptides.name: Semaglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist)
peptides.how: weekly subcutaneous or daily oral, physician-titrated
peptides.effect: meaningfully lowers fasting glucose plus weight loss
peptides.caution: FDA-approved peptide (Ozempic/Rybelsus) but prescription / physician-supervised only; risks: nausea/vomiting, pancreatitis, gallbladder disease; contraindicated with personal/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2

peptides.name: Tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist)
peptides.effect: strongly lowers fasting glucose plus substantial weight loss
peptides.caution: FDA-approved peptide (Mounjaro) but prescription / physician-supervised only; risks: GI effects, pancreatitis, gallbladder; same medullary thyroid carcinoma/MEN2 contraindication

peptides.name: Retatrutide (triple GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonist)
peptides.effect: lowered fasting glucose markedly in phase 2/3 trials
peptides.caution: NOT FDA-approved / investigational; long-term safety unestablished; GI effects and transient heart-rate rise; requires medical supervision

waist.elite_note: Lower waist circumference reflects less visceral fat. Common risk thresholds: >102 cm men / >88 cm women (lower for South/East Asian ancestry, ~90 cm men / ~80 cm women). Waist-to-height ratio <0.5 is a practical target. Visceral fat is more prognostic than subcutaneous, so diet + exercise combined outperform either alone.

diet_exercise.name: Sustained caloric deficit via high-protein Mediterranean pattern
diet_exercise.how: modest calorie deficit; cut alcohol, sugar-sweetened beverages and refined carbs; prioritize protein & fiber
diet_exercise.effect: reduces waist circumference and visceral fat
diet_exercise.caution: adherence is the main limiter; avoid excessively low-calorie crash dieting that erodes lean mass

diet_exercise.name: Aerobic exercise (incl. HIIT) + resistance training
diet_exercise.how: 150-300 min/week aerobic plus 2-3 strength sessions
diet_exercise.effect: reduces visceral adipose tissue, sometimes even with little scale-weight change
diet_exercise.caution: progress gradually; combine modalities for best central-fat effect

diet_exercise.name: Adequate sleep + stress/cortisol management
diet_exercise.how: 7-9 h regular sleep; stress-reduction practices
diet_exercise.effect: short sleep and chronic stress associate with greater central adiposity; correcting them supports waist reduction
diet_exercise.caution: evaluate for sleep apnea if indicated

supplements.name: Viscous soluble fiber (psyllium 7-10 g/day; glucomannan 2-4 g/day)
supplements.how: taken before meals with ample water
supplements.effect: modest waist reduction (~1-2 cm) and small weight loss over 8-12 weeks
supplements.caution: OTC; take with plenty of water (glucomannan carries choking/GI-obstruction risk if taken dry); bloating; separate from medications/other supplements by ~2 h

supplements.name: Green tea catechins (EGCG) ± caffeine
supplements.how: standardized extract or brewed green tea
supplements.effect: small, inconsistent reductions in body weight/waist, greater when paired with exercise
supplements.caution: high-dose EGCG extracts linked to rare hepatotoxicity; caffeine can disturb sleep/raise blood pressure

supplements.name: Whey/protein supplementation
supplements.how: 20-40 g/day to reach protein targets in a deficit
supplements.effect: supports waist reduction indirectly by preserving lean mass and improving satiety/body composition
supplements.caution: counts toward daily calories; caution in advanced kidney disease

drugs.name: Phentermine/topiramate ER (Qsymia)
drugs.how: physician-titrated daily dosing
drugs.effect: reduces body weight and waist circumference
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; teratogenic (topiramate—avoid in pregnancy), raised heart rate, paresthesia/cognitive effects; phentermine is a controlled substance

drugs.name: Orlistat
drugs.how: 120 mg with fat-containing meals (60 mg OTC dose available)
drugs.effect: modest weight and waist reduction via dietary-fat malabsorption
drugs.caution: prescription (also lower-dose OTC) / physician-supervised; oily stools/steatorrhea, malabsorption of fat-soluble vitamins—supplement them

drugs.name: Naltrexone/bupropion (Contrave)
drugs.how: physician-titrated combination
drugs.effect: modest weight and waist reduction
drugs.caution: prescription / physician-supervised; seizure risk, raised blood pressure/heart rate, psychiatric/mood effects; avoid with seizure disorder or chronic opioid use

peptides.name: Tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist)
peptides.effect: large waist reduction secondary to ~15-22% weight loss
peptides.caution: FDA-approved peptide (Zepbound/Mounjaro) but prescription / physician-supervised only; risks: GI effects, pancreatitis, gallbladder; medullary thyroid carcinoma/MEN2 contraindication

peptides.name: Tesamorelin (GHRH analog)
peptides.effect: selectively reduces visceral adipose tissue ~15-20% over 26 weeks (subcutaneous fat largely unchanged)
peptides.caution: FDA-approved ONLY for HIV-associated lipodystrophy; general anti-aging/visceral-fat use is off-label/experimental and requires physician supervision; risks: raised IGF-1, glucose intolerance/worsened insulin resistance, injection-site reactions, edema/arthralgia; contraindicated in active malignancy or pregnancy

peptides.name: Retatrutide (triple GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonist)
peptides.effect: produced ~17-24% weight loss with marked waist reduction in trials
peptides.caution: NOT FDA-approved / investigational; long-term safety unknown; GI effects and heart-rate rise; trials or gray-market only, requires medical supervision

hemoglobin.elite_note: Elite is mid-normal (roughly men ~14-15, women ~13-14 g/dL), not maximal. Low Hb usually = iron/B12/folate deficiency or blood loss; high Hb = dehydration, smoking, sleep apnea, testosterone therapy, or polycythemia. Confirm ferritin, B12/folate, hydration and EPO context before acting. No legitimate peptide raises Hb safely; EPO-type agents are prescription biologics listed under drugs.

diet_exercise.name: Iron- and B-vitamin-rich diet (+ vitamin C foods)
diet_exercise.how: Heme iron (lean red meat, poultry, fish) plus non-heme (legumes, leafy greens) eaten with citrus/peppers; adequate dietary B12 and folate
diet_exercise.effect: raises Hb when it is low from nutritional deficiency; corrects nutritional anemia
diet_exercise.caution: only helps if intake/absorption is the limiter; tea/coffee and calcium with meals inhibit iron absorption

diet_exercise.name: Correct hypoxic drivers and hydration (for high Hb)
diet_exercise.how: Smoking cessation, treat obstructive sleep apnea (CPAP), weight loss; maintain steady euhydration
diet_exercise.effect: lowers or normalizes an elevated Hb driven by chronic hypoxia or plasma-volume contraction
diet_exercise.caution: distinguish relative (dehydration) from absolute erythrocytosis before assuming a cause

diet_exercise.name: Regular aerobic/endurance training
diet_exercise.how: 150+ min/week moderate aerobic exercise; altitude exposure increases hemoglobin mass
diet_exercise.effect: supports healthy red-cell mass and can modestly raise Hb over months; note plasma-volume expansion can transiently lower measured Hb
diet_exercise.caution: dilutional 'athlete's pseudoanemia' is not true anemia

supplements.name: Oral iron
supplements.how: Ferrous sulfate/bisglycinate ~40-100 mg elemental; alternate-day dosing often better absorbed and tolerated
supplements.effect: raises Hb in iron-deficiency anemia over weeks to months
supplements.caution: use only if ferritin/transferrin saturation is low; GI upset/constipation; iron overload risk if not truly deficient, so test first

supplements.name: Vitamin B12 and/or folate
supplements.how: Repletion of low B12 (methyl/cyanocobalamin) and/or folate (folic acid or 5-MTHF)
supplements.effect: corrects megaloblastic anemia, raising Hb
supplements.caution: rule out B12 deficiency before high-dose folate to avoid masking neurologic B12 deficiency

supplements.name: Vitamin C with iron
supplements.how: ~200-500 mg taken with the iron dose
supplements.effect: enhances non-heme iron absorption; meta-analyses show only a small added Hb gain (~0.1 g/dL) over iron alone
supplements.caution: clinically minor benefit; not essential

drugs.name: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (epoetin alfa, darbepoetin alfa)
drugs.how: Prescription injectable ESA for anemia of chronic kidney disease or chemotherapy
drugs.effect: raises Hb in renal or chemotherapy-induced anemia
drugs.caution: PRESCRIPTION/physician-supervised only; black-box risk of thrombosis, stroke, MI, death and tumor progression; not for otherwise-healthy optimization

drugs.name: IV iron (ferric carboxymaltose, iron sucrose)
drugs.how: Prescription infusion when oral iron fails/is not tolerated or rapid repletion is needed
drugs.effect: raises Hb in iron-deficiency anemia
drugs.caution: PRESCRIPTION/physician-supervised; rare hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis and hypophosphatemia

drugs.name: Therapeutic phlebotomy (for high Hb)
drugs.how: Physician-directed venesection; typical target Hct <52-54% in symptomatic secondary erythrocytosis or TRT-induced elevation
drugs.effect: lowers an elevated Hb/Hct
drugs.caution: PHYSICIAN-supervised procedure (not a drug); causes iron depletion; reserved for symptomatic or markedly high values

mcv.elite_note: MCV is a diagnostic clue, not a value to manipulate directly; normalize it (85-92 fL) by fixing the cause. High MCV (>~92-100): alcohol, B12/folate deficiency, hypothyroidism, liver disease, myelodysplasia. Low MCV (<~80): iron deficiency, thalassemia trait. Order B12, folate, MMA/homocysteine, TSH and reticulocytes before supplementing. No peptide is applicable.

diet_exercise.name: Reduce or eliminate alcohol
diet_exercise.how: Abstinence or marked reduction in intake
diet_exercise.effect: lowers alcohol-driven macrocytosis; MCV normalizes over roughly 2-4 months (red-cell lifespan)
diet_exercise.caution: alcohol is a leading cause of high MCV via direct marrow toxicity, independent of nutrition

diet_exercise.name: B12/folate-rich diet (high MCV) or iron-rich diet (low MCV)
diet_exercise.how: Animal/fortified foods for B12 and leafy greens/legumes for folate; heme iron if microcytic
diet_exercise.effect: moves MCV toward 85-92 by correcting the underlying nutritional deficiency

supplements.name: Vitamin B12
supplements.how: Methyl/cyanocobalamin orally (high-dose if malabsorptive) when B12 is low/borderline with elevated MMA
supplements.effect: lowers an elevated MCV by reversing megaloblastic change
supplements.caution: check B12/MMA first; untreated B12 deficiency risks irreversible neuropathy

supplements.name: Folate (folic acid or 5-MTHF)
supplements.effect: lowers an elevated MCV caused by folate deficiency
supplements.caution: NEVER give folate alone before excluding B12 deficiency, as it corrects the anemia while masking and allowing progression of B12 neurologic damage

supplements.name: Iron (if MCV is low/microcytic)
supplements.effect: raises a low MCV back toward normal
supplements.caution: test-guided; not for high MCV

drugs.name: Parenteral B12 (hydroxocobalamin injection)
drugs.how: IM B12 for pernicious anemia or malabsorption
drugs.effect: normalizes a high MCV from B12 deficiency when oral is inadequate
drugs.caution: PRESCRIPTION/physician-supervised

drugs.name: Levothyroxine (if hypothyroid)
drugs.how: Thyroid hormone replacement for hypothyroidism-related macrocytosis
drugs.effect: helps normalize MCV when hypothyroidism is the cause
drugs.caution: PRESCRIPTION/physician-supervised; titrate to TSH

lymph_pct.elite_note: A low lymphocyte percentage (lymphopenia) tracks with infection risk, frailty and mortality; the elite target is a robust ~30-40% with a healthy CD4:CD8 profile. Persistent lymphopenia deserves a workup (chronic infection, corticosteroids, marrow/immune disorders) rather than supplements alone. No FDA-approved drug safely raises lymphocytes in healthy people.

diet_exercise.name: Regular moderate exercise (aerobic + resistance)
diet_exercise.how: ~150 min/week aerobic plus 2 resistance sessions; avoid chronic overtraining
diet_exercise.effect: improves the T-cell profile and can raise total lymphocytes while reducing senescent T cells with sustained training; effect on percentage is modest and variable
diet_exercise.caution: a bout of intense exercise transiently drops circulating lymphocytes, and overtraining suppresses immunity

diet_exercise.name: Adequate sleep and stress reduction
diet_exercise.how: 7-9 h sleep nightly; reduce chronic psychological stress and cortisol load
diet_exercise.effect: supports lymphocyte numbers, since chronic cortisol elevation lowers lymphocytes

diet_exercise.name: Sufficient protein and energy intake
diet_exercise.how: Adequate protein-calorie nutrition; treat undernutrition
diet_exercise.effect: prevents and helps reverse malnutrition-associated lymphopenia

supplements.name: Zinc (if deficient or older adult)
supplements.effect: raises T-lymphocyte counts and the CD4:CD8 ratio in zinc-deficiency states
supplements.caution: do not exceed ~40 mg/day; excess zinc causes copper deficiency and can itself impair immunity

supplements.name: Vitamin D (if deficient)
supplements.effect: modest increases in circulating T cells (CD3/CD4) seen in trials of deficient or overweight subjects
supplements.caution: correct deficiency only; avoid megadoses

supplements.name: General micronutrient repletion (B-vitamins, protein/whey)
supplements.how: Address any documented deficiency limiting immune cell production
supplements.effect: supports lymphopoiesis when a specific deficiency is the limiter

peptides.name: Thymosin alpha-1 (thymalfasin)
peptides.how: Physician-administered subcutaneous thymic peptide that stimulates T-cell maturation
peptides.effect: raises CD4 and absolute lymphocyte counts and improves CD4:CD8 in immunocompromised patients (disease-context data)
peptides.caution: NOT FDA-approved in the US (approved in 30+ other countries; US investigational/orphan); experimental for healthy longevity use; requires medical supervision; risk of injection-site reactions and theoretical autoimmune over-stimulation, with unproven long-term safety

peptides.name: Thymalin / thymic peptide extracts
peptides.effect: claimed to raise T-lymphocytes, but based on sparse, largely older/Russian data
peptides.caution: NOT FDA-approved; minimal controlled human evidence and unregulated purity; requires medical supervision

sedentary_frac.elite_note: A lower sedentary fraction—especially breaking up prolonged uninterrupted sitting—is protective for mortality and cardiometabolic health partly independent of MVPA. Behavioral interventions are clearly first-line; no supplement, drug, or peptide is credibly established to reduce sedentary behavior.

diet_exercise.name: Sit-stand / active workstation with prompts
diet_exercise.how: Alternate sitting and standing; standing or treadmill desk paired with reminders/promotion
diet_exercise.effect: Reduces occupational sitting by roughly 40-100 min/day (network meta-analysis of RCTs), more when combined with behavioral prompts
diet_exercise.caution: Increase standing time gradually to avoid leg, foot, or back discomfort

diet_exercise.name: Regularly break up prolonged sitting ('sitting breaks')
diet_exercise.how: Stand or move 2-5 min every ~30 min; take an hourly short walk
diet_exercise.effect: Lowers total sedentary fraction and improves postprandial glucose/insulin
diet_exercise.caution: None major

diet_exercise.name: Wearable inactivity prompts + stand/step goals
diet_exercise.how: Enable move/stand reminders on a tracker; set daily stand and light-activity goals
diet_exercise.effect: Reduces sedentary time and increases light-intensity activity
diet_exercise.caution: Effect can attenuate; refresh goals and prompts periodically
